poems:
At the fish market the ice arrives before the fish.
Somebody has already been wrong about how much ice.

4:01.
The paper mill has been running since Tuesday
and holds no opinion about Thursday.
Yellow bucket of chlorine tablets, motel pool gate.
Somewhere a man puts on the second sock and calls it progress.

He backs out with the headlights off so the house stays out of it.
Ninety miles.
He has done this for eleven years.

Turn the key.
Don't rev it.
The neighbor works nights and just got in.

4:06. The dog has decided this is morning.
The dog is outvoted.

In the milking parlor the radio plays for the cows.
Country station.
Their preference was never surveyed.
One glove on the on-ramp shoulder.

The baby is finally down.
Nobody moves.
The floorboard by the closet is a known informant.
4:10, and the bakers are three hours in and starting to talk again.

Proof, n.
What dough does when left alone.
Also what nobody asks the baker for.

Room 412 buzzes.
The nurse is already standing.
She was standing before it buzzed.
A hand truck chained to a bike rack outside a bar that closed at two.

If you are up because of a decision, it is too early to make it.
If you are up because of a noise, it was the ice maker.

DIESEL  41.2 GAL
SHOWER  1
BANANA  2
DRIVE SAFE
The crane lifts a box out of one country's paperwork and into another's.

Nobody chooses 4:17.
It is arrived at.

The farmer would like it understood that he is not up early.
He is simply up.

The white truck idles at the end of the gravel,
headlights picking out the gate.

4:20.
Yes.
Somewhere.
Congratulations.
The bread aisle is restocked by a man who will never watch anyone eat it.

Two more hours of sleep is not two hours.
It is one hour, then the arithmetic.

The night auditor closes out the day whenever he decides to.
He picks now.
One traffic cone, an empty parking deck.
The ramp crew loads bags for a flight that will later be described as morning.

4:26. Somewhere the first bird has an opinion.
Not a song yet.
An opinion.

REFRIGERATE AFTER OPENING.
Nothing here has been opened.
Nothing here has been closed either.

He still makes two cups.
He drinks one and lets the other go cold on the sill.
Count clears. Everyone is where the paperwork says.
4:30. The alarms of the disciplined and the alarms of the doomed sound identical.
Through the floor, a voice: I'm up, I'm up, I'm up.
A raccoon on the dumpster lid, mid-decision.
Mid-ocean, the cabin stays dark and the crew speaks in the register saved for babies and animals.

The dialysis center opens at five.
The first car has been in the lot since four.
4:35, and the schedule you made last night reads like something written by a stranger with real confidence.
The hydraulic whine two streets over is somebody else's problem for another forty seconds.

A bicycle chained to a sign
that says no bicycles.
The rink is resurfaced for children who will not arrive until eight.

Wallet.
Badge.
Phone.
Keys.
Lunch.
The lunch is the one that gets left.
At 4:40 the body runs its coldest and has arranged for the blanket to be one inch short.
An oven timer three houses down runs its whole routine for nobody.
The cat has slept eleven hours. It continues.
If you haven't slept, the plan is to keep going and be strange about it later.
Wet newspaper, plastic sleeve, end of the driveway.
4:45. First bus out of the yard, empty, doors opening at every stop anyway.

Commuter, n.
One who leaves in the dark to arrive before the day has been agreed on.

4:47. In a port city ahead of us,
longshoremen are arguing about lunch.

The heat lamps in the farrowing barn stay on.
Nobody consults the season.
Two pairs of boots by the screen door.
4:50. The shower starts upstairs and the house revises its opinion of itself.

Whatever you decided at two is still here.
It waited.
It brought notes.

Third shift starts thinking about the drive home.
Eighty minutes.
They think about it early.

PLEASE RING BELL FOR NIGHT SERVICE.
Someone has put tape over the bell.

The gym unlocks at five.
The lot already has a quorum.

4:55. The coffee maker clicks on by itself,
loyal to last night's optimism.

4:56. The register shuts.
The lot goes back to being empty.

The rooster is not announcing anything.
The rooster has no information.

Bread comes out.
The smell reaches the sidewalk and finds nobody to work on.

4:59. The day is still a rumor.
The kettle is the first to repeat it.
